message.content:
Here are some of the most popular and highly regarded sushi restaurants in Tokyo:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights |
|------------|----------|------------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza (and other branches) | Legendary chef Jiro Ono; Michelin‑starred; famed for precision and traditional Edomae style. |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato | Intimate setting (only 8 seats); three Michelin stars; renowned for impeccable nigiri and service. |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza | Three Michelin stars; focuses on seasonal ingredients and subtle flavors. |
| **Sushi Mizutani** | Ginza | Two Michelin stars; known for its minimalist décor and high‑quality fish. |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Popular spot for fresh tuna; long lines but worth the wait. |
| **Sushi Zanmai** | Multiple locations | Casual, open‑air counter; great for late‑night sushi and affordable prices. |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | Classic Edo‑style sushi; offers both lunch and dinner menus. |
| **Sushi Sawada** | Ginza | Known for its “sashimi” style and creative rolls. |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Shinjuku | Small, intimate, and highly praised for its freshness. |
| **Sushi Tsubaki** | Roppongi | Offers a modern twist on traditional sushi; excellent omakase experience. |

If you’re planning a visit, it’s wise to make reservations well in advance—especially for the Michelin‑starred spots—and be prepared for potential waiting lists at the more casual venues. Enjoy your sushi adventure!
